why: A photo-printing service whose customers place 1.2 to 5.9 orders of roughly $28 to $32 each in 90 days, earning a first-year profit of $0.6 to $19 per customer, is believable.
Each rating distribution for both groups adds to 100%, and 25,000 shoppers tasting a new drink in stores is a believable programme.
Twelve teams with 350 brokers bringing in $133 million, about $380,000 per broker, is believable for a ship-broking firm.
Direct and indirect parts add to each bar's total, and a combined 2.2 percentage-point lift to GDP growth from VC over ten years is believable.
A uniform rental leader with 2,900 staff and about $520 million a year in revenue (around $180,000 per employee), whose margin slips while industry profits rise, is believable.
Overseas market shares of 0.3% to 7.3% fit a firm that 'sells little' abroad, and margins up to about 44% are high for paint but within a factor of a few of what it could report.
A commercial washer using 1,100 to 1,400 kWh a year at 12c per kWh, serviced 3 to 6 times a year by a $16-an-hour technician, is believable.
Roughly 2.2 to 2.7 potter-hours per hand-thrown bowl is slow but within a factor of a few for a small studio, and 0.5 plus 2 extra potters giving 2.5 is consistent.
New and existing parts add to each service's total, and about 3.3% average yearly revenue growth for a telecoms company is believable.
About an hour of groomer time per dog (79 hours for 77 dogs, 395 hours for 367 dogs) is believable for a pet shop's grooming service.
